title: CEREBELLAR ATAXIA, IMPAIRED INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENT, AND DYSEQUILIBRIUM SYNDROME 4
alt_titles: CEREBELLAR ATAXIA AND MENTAL RETARDATION WITH OR WITHOUT QUADRUPEDAL LOCOMOTION 4
CEREBELLAR ATAXIA, MENTAL RETARDATION, AND DYSEQUILIBRIUM SYNDROME 4

relationships.phenotype: CEREBELLAR ATAXIA, IMPAIRED INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENT, AND DYSEQUILIBRIUM SYNDROME 4

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysequilibrium syndrome-4 (CAMRQ4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ATP8A2 gene (605870) on chromosome 13q12.

checks.claim: Cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysequilibrium syndrome-4 (CAMRQ4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ATP8A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Altogether, 6 of the 7 homozygous or compound heterozygous missense mutations known in ATP8A2 located in this subregion (amino acids 364‐877) of the catalytic cytoplasmic domain.
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous and compound heterozygous ATP8A2 mutations to CAMRQ4.

checks.claim: The ATP8A2 gene is located on chromosome 13q12.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping revealed that several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12.
checks.explanation: The abstract places the linked homozygous region, which contains ATP8A2, at 13q12.

paragraphs.text: CAMRQ4 is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder. Its main features are congenital cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysarthria. Some affected individuals walk on all four limbs (quadrupedal locomotion). Severe hypotonia, abnormal involuntary movements such as chorea, and optic atrophy have also been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.

checks.claim: CAMRQ4 is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The pattern of inheritance in all of the possible phenotypes is autosomal recessive.
checks.explanation: The abstract also calls CAMRQ an early-onset neurodevelopmental disorder.

checks.claim: The main features of CAMRQ4 are congenital cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation and dysequilibrium syndrome is a rare and heterogeneous condition.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions ataxia and mental retardation. It does not mention dysarthria and does not say the ataxia is congenital.

checks.claim: Some individuals with CAMRQ4 walk on all four limbs (quadrupedal locomotion).
checks.evidence_quote: is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.explanation: The title links the disorder to quadrupedal locomotion.

checks.claim: Severe hypotonia has been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: The first noticeable clinical sign was severe neonatal hypotonia.
checks.explanation: This describes the proband with an ATP8A2 mutation. The abstract also reports severe hypotonia.

checks.claim: Abnormal involuntary movements such as chorea have been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Japanese siblings presented with athetotic movements at 1 and 2 months of age.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports athetotic involuntary movements. Chorea is not mentioned specifically.

checks.claim: Optic atrophy has been reported in patients with ATP8A2 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Besides, more severe phenotypes with optic atrophy, absence of ambulation, unhealthy brain MRI, non‐verbal or absent speech, and feeding difficulties have also been reported.
checks.explanation: Table 1 also records optic atrophy in previously reported ATP8A2 patients.

paragraphs.text: Onat et al. (2013) described a consanguineous Turkish family in which several sibs had cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysarthria. Affected members walked quadrupedally. Brain imaging showed cerebellar atrophy.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) described a consanguineous Turkish family in which several sibs had cerebellar ataxia, impaired intellectual development, and dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms a consanguineous Turkish family with four affected members. It does not say they are sibs and does not mention dysarthria.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous Turkish family described by Onat et al. (2013) walked quadrupedally.
checks.evidence_quote: Missense mutation in the ATPase, aminophospholipid transporter protein ATP8A2 is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.explanation: The title links the family's mutation to quadrupedal locomotion.

checks.claim: Brain imaging of affected members of the consanguineous Turkish family described by Onat et al. (2013) showed cerebellar atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: is associated with cerebellar atrophy and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.explanation: The title mentions cerebellar atrophy, but the abstract does not describe any brain imaging.

paragraphs.text: Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) reported patients with ATP8A2 mutations who had a severe encephalopathy with impaired intellectual development, marked hypotonia, chorea, and optic atrophy. This broadened the phenotype linked to the gene.

checks.claim: Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) reported patients with ATP8A2 mutations who had a severe encephalopathy with impaired intellectual development, marked hypotonia, chorea, and optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Martin‐Hernandez et al, 2016
checks.explanation: In Table 1, the Martin-Hernandez column records encephalopathy, intellectual disability, hypotonia and optic atrophy as 'Yes'. Chorea is not mentioned, and the encephalopathy is not described as severe.

checks.claim: The report by Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) broadened the phenotype linked to ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract (only text supplied) does not mention ATP8A2 or any broadening of its phenotype. The paper is about VLDLR.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CAMRQ4 in the family reported by Onat et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of CAMRQ4 in the family reported by Onat et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a consanguineous family from Turkey with four affected individuals exhibiting the condition. Homozygosity mapping revealed
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance follows from consanguinity and homozygosity mapping, but the abstract does not state the inheritance pattern.

paragraphs.text: Cacciagli et al. (2010) reported a patient with severe impaired intellectual development and major hypotonia who carried a de novo balanced translocation involving chromosome 13. The breakpoint disrupted the ATP8A2 gene.

checks.claim: Cacciagli et al. (2010) reported a patient with severe impaired intellectual development and major hypotonia who carried a de novo balanced translocation involving chromosome 13.
checks.evidence_quote: an unrelated individual has been identified, in whom mental retardation and severe hypotonia is associated with a de novo t(10;13) balanced translocation resulting with the disruption of ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes this patient but does not name Cacciagli et al. (2010) as the source. It also does not say the intellectual disability was severe.

checks.claim: The translocation breakpoint in the patient reported by Cacciagli et al. (2010) disrupted the ATP8A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo balanced translocation t(10;13) interrupting the ATP8A2 coding sequence was detected
checks.explanation: The translocation is stated to interrupt the ATP8A2 coding sequence.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of the consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ, Onat et al. (2013) found a homozygous missense mutation in the ATP8A2 gene (I376M). They identified it using homozygosity mapping followed by sequencing. The mutation segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) found a homozygous missense mutation (I376M) in the ATP8A2 gene in affected members of a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The I376M missense variant in a consanguineous Turkish family is stated. Homozygosity is implied by the homozygosity mapping but not stated outright in the abstract.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) identified the ATP8A2 I376M mutation using homozygosity mapping followed by sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity mapping revealed that several shared homozygous regions, including chromosome 13q12. Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis
checks.explanation: The abstract describes homozygosity mapping followed by targeted sequencing.

checks.claim: The ATP8A2 I376M mutation segregated with the disorder in the consanguineous Turkish family reported by Onat et al. (2013).
checks.evidence_quote: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: A segregation analysis was done and supported the variant.

paragraphs.text: Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) identified homozygous or compound heterozygous ATP8A2 mutations in patients with severe hypotonia, chorea, optic atrophy, and impaired intellectual development.

checks.claim: Martin-Hernandez et al. (2016) identified homozygous or compound heterozygous ATP8A2 mutations in patients with severe hypotonia, chorea, optic atrophy, and impaired intellectual development.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract (only text supplied) does not mention ATP8A2 mutations. It reports homozygous VLDLR mutations (R257X and c2339delT) in families with quadrupedal gait.

paragraphs.text: Zhu et al. (2012) found that the mouse 'wabbler-lethal' phenotype is caused by mutations in the Atp8a2 gene. Affected mice had ataxia and axonal degeneration.

checks.claim: Zhu et al. (2012) found that the mouse 'wabbler-lethal' phenotype is caused by mutations in the Atp8a2 gene.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract (only text supplied) does not mention the wabbler-lethal mouse, Atp8a2 or Zhu et al. (2012).

checks.claim: Wabbler-lethal mice with Atp8a2 mutations had ataxia and axonal degeneration.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract (only text supplied) does not mention mouse models, ataxia in mice or axonal degeneration.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ4 and quadrupedal locomotion, Onat et al. (2013) identified a homozygous ile376-to-met (I376M) substitution in the ATP8A2 gene. The mutation segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: Onat et al. (2013) identified a homozygous ile376-to-met (I376M) substitution in the ATP8A2 gene in affected members of a consanguineous Turkish family with CAMRQ4 and quadrupedal locomotion.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: The variant, the family and the quadrupedal locomotion are all supported. Homozygosity is implied by the homozygosity mapping but not stated outright in the abstract.

checks.claim: The ATP8A2 I376M substitution segregated with CAMRQ4 in the consanguineous Turkish family reported by Onat et al. (2013).
checks.evidence_quote: Targeted next-generation sequencing of an affected individual followed by segregation analysis, population screening and prediction approaches revealed a novel missense variant, p.I376M, in ATP8A2.
checks.explanation: A segregation analysis was done and supported the variant.
